title: DOJ data analytics flag a $10.6 billion catheter billing scheme; CMS withholds $4.41 billion (Operation Gold Rush)
summary: DOJ's 2025 Health Care Fraud Takedown says its Data Analytics Team detected anomalous billing by a transnational organization and that HHS-OIG and CMS prevented all but $41 million of $4.45 billion...
account: The Department of Justice's press release of 30 June 2025 announced the 2025 National Health Care Fraud Takedown. It covered 324 defendants and over $14.6 billion in intended loss. The release describes Operation Gold Rush. An organization allegedly used foreign straw owners to buy dozens of medical supply companies. It submitted $10.6 billion in fraudulent Medicare claims for urinary catheters and other durable medical equipment. The claims used the stolen identities of over one million Americans. Per the release, the Health Care Fraud Unit's Data Analytics Team and its partners detected the anomalous billing through proactive data analytics. Medicare was scheduled to pay approximately $4.45 billion. HHS-OIG and CMS prevented the organization from receiving all but approximately $41 million of it, per the release. HHS and CMS intend to return the $4.41 billion in escrow to the Medicare trust fund. Medicare supplemental insurers still paid approximately $900 million. Nineteen defendants were charged and twelve arrested, four in Estonia. The Data Analytics Team was established in 2018, the release says. It announces a Health Care Fraud Data Fusion Center to leverage cloud computing, artificial intelligence and advanced analytics. It does not say that AI or machine learning was used in the Gold Rush detection.

ratings.reason: The release states that $4.41 billion scheduled to be paid by Medicare was held in escrow for return to the Medicare trust fund. Supplemental insurers still paid about $900 million.
CMS and HHS-OIG stopped payment of all but about $41 million of $4.45 billion in claims from the organization, per the release.
The release describes over one million stolen identities but documents no outcome for the individual beneficiaries.

ai_role.statement: The detection is attributed to the Data Analytics Team's proactive data analytics. No statement says that AI or machine learning was involved. The Fusion Center that will use artificial intelligence is announced as future work. Developer and deployer of the analytics are the same public body, DOJ's Health Care Fraud Unit, acting with HHS-OIG and CMS.

later.note: On 3 February 2026 a Brooklyn bank relationship manager pleaded guilty to conspiring to launder more than $8 million of proceeds of the scheme uncovered by Operation Gold Rush, with sentencing set for 20 April 2026.
later.quote: According to court documents, Renat Abramov, 36, of Brooklyn, a former relationship manager at a U.S. bank branch in Sheepshead Bay, used his position to aid a sophisticated international scheme uncovered by Operation Gold Rush.
